name: A subspace of $\real^4$
text:
Suppose we have the 4-dimensional vectors $\vvec_1$, $\vvec_2$, and $\vvec_3$ that define the subspace $S = \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}$ of $\real^4$. Suppose also that $$ \begin{bmatrix} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp -1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$ From the reduced row echelon form of the matrix, we see that $\vvec_2 = -\vvec_1$. Therefore, any linear combination of $\vvec_1$, $\vvec_2$, and $\vvec_3$ can be rewritten $$ c_1\vvec_1 + c_2\vvec_2 + c_3 \vvec_3 = (c_1-c_2)\vvec_1 + c_2\vvec_3 $$ as a linear combination of $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_3$. This tells us that $$ S = \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3} = \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_3}. $$

Furthermore, the reduced row echelon form of the matrix shows that $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_3$ are linearly independent. Therefore, $\{\vvec_1,\vvec_3\}$ is a basis for $S$, which means that $S$ is a two-dimensional subspace of $\real^4$.
